title: Apply ordered dual-stack CIDR rules
prompt: Implement solve(payload) using only local IP parsing. rules is an ordered list of {"cidr":string,"action":"allow"|"deny"}, default is "allow" or "deny", and addresses is a list of strings. Parse CIDRs with host bits allowed and masked (Python ipaddress.ip_network(...,strict=False) semantics). The first matching rule decides, regardless of prefix length; IPv4 and IPv6 never match across families, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. Return {"decisions":[ "allow"|"deny"|"invalid", ...]} in address order. Invalid address text produces "invalid". Invalid CIDR, invalid rule action or invalid default returns {"error":"invalid_rule"} before any decisions. No DNS or network I/O is permitted. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 0, relative tolerance 0; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
